title: Citation enforcement, abstention and answerability
summary: Answerability decides whether the evidence can answer at all, citation enforcement forces each claim to point at a source span, and abstention is the safe response when it cannot.
useIf: A confident wrong answer costs more than "I could not find that", and users or auditors need to trace claims to sources.
avoidIf: The assistant is a creative or brainstorming tool where no source of truth exists.

explain.md: Three checks sound alike and differ. **Answerability** asks before generation whether the retrieved evidence is sufficient. **Citation validity** asks after generation whether each citation points at a real span. **Support** asks whether that span entails the claim. A citation proves **provenance**, not **entailment**, so you still need a check such as NLI or quote verification. ALCE is a benchmark for answers with citations, and AIS (Attributable to Identified Sources) is an annotation framework for whether output is supported by a source [[r22]] [[r23]].

**API-native citations** help: Anthropic's Citations feature is enabled with `citations` on `document` or `search_result` blocks, returns types such as `char_location`, `page_location` and `content_block_location`, does not count `cited_text` toward output tokens and works with prompt caching, token counting and batch. It is incompatible with structured outputs: enabling both returns HTTP 400 [[r24]]. **Prompt-based** enforcement asks for word-for-word quotes first on long documents and gives explicit permission to say "I don't know" [[r23]].

**Abstention thresholds** need care. Azure's semantic reranker score runs from 0 to 4, and it only reorders the top 50 candidates, so poor recall before reranking cannot be fixed by a threshold [[tr1]]. Scores drift across model updates, so use coarse cut-offs and re-test after changes. Corrective RAG adds a retrieval evaluator that triggers a fallback when retrieved evidence looks poor, a pattern you can reuse for abstention [[r25]]. Good abstention is useful: say what is missing and offer a next step.

explain.title: Answerable, cited, supported or abstain
explain.alt: A question is retrieved, an answerability gate decides, the model generates with citations, and a support check validates the cited spans. Failures at either gate lead to abstention or repair.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  Q[Question] --> R[Retrieve]
  R --> A{Answerable}
  A -->|yes| G[Generate with citations]
  G --> V{Spans support claims}
  V -->|yes| O[Answer]
  V -->|no| X[Abstain or repair]
  A -->|no| X

whereToUse: Regulated assistants where every statement must be traceable to a document
Customer support bots that must not invent policies or prices
Search-plus-summary products that show source links
Enterprise Q&A where "no answer found" is a valid, logged outcome
Evaluation suites that score citation precision and recall

use: Use an answerability gate when retrieval often returns weak evidence
Use API-native or schema-based citations so every claim carries a span reference
Use support checks (NLI, quote match) because citations alone are not proof
Use coarse retrieval-score cut-offs plus a measured abstention rate
avoid: Avoid treating the presence of a citation as evidence of correctness
Avoid hard-coded fine thresholds on reranker scores that drift
Avoid abstaining with a bare refusal: offer a next step
flips: You need structured JSON output: Anthropic citations return HTTP 400 with it, so put quote and source fields in your schema and verify them
Retrieval is high quality and the domain is low risk: a prompt permitting "I don't know" may replace a separate gate
False abstentions hurt more than errors: answer with a caveat and a confidence label instead of refusing

alternatives.title: Compared with its neighbours
head: Technique
Wins when
Loses when
Cost or risk
rows: Schema fields for quote and source id
A cheap first signal for no-answer

pitfalls.symptom: Citations look right but the cited passage does not support the claim
pitfalls.fix: Verify the quote exists and run an entailment check against the cited span

pitfalls.symptom: Requests fail with HTTP 400 after turning on citations
pitfalls.cause: Anthropic citations cannot be combined with structured outputs
pitfalls.fix: Use schema fields for quotes and sources or run formatting as a separate step

pitfalls.symptom: Abstention rate jumps after a ranker update
pitfalls.cause: A fine-grained score cut-off was tuned on the old score distribution
pitfalls.fix: Use coarse thresholds, re-test after model changes and alert on abstention drift

pitfalls.cause: Over-abstention on a query type the threshold was never tuned for
pitfalls.fix: Measure false abstentions per query type and answer with caveats where risk allows

scenarios.title: Benefits guidance in a regulated setting
scenarios.situation: An assistant explains benefits rules to staff. A wrong answer can lead to a compliance incident. Retrieval sometimes returns weakly related chunks. An extra second of latency is fine.
unknowns: How often is the evidence insufficient?
Is there a human escalation route?
scenarios.question: How do you enforce evidence?

options.name: Answerability gate, citations required on every claim, span support check, abstain with escalation
options.why: It stops unsupported answers at three points and leaves an audit trail.
options.tradeoff: More latency and some false abstentions.

options.name: Prompt asking the model to cite and say "I don't know"
options.why: Nothing verifies that spans exist or support claims, so wrong answers pass.

options.name: Citations plus a reranker-score cut-off
options.why: Cheap and removes the weakest cases.
options.tradeoff: Does not test support, and the cut-off drifts with ranker updates.

flips.if: Stakes drop to a general FAQ
flips.then: A prompt with citations and a coarse cut-off is enough.
Answer with caveats where a claim is partially supported.

scenarios.takeaway: In high-stakes domains, verify support and design the abstention path.

scenarios.title: Extraction pipeline with JSON output
scenarios.situation: A pipeline extracts obligations from policy documents into JSON for a database. Each field must reference the source text. The team planned to use API-native citations.
unknowns: Are quotes short enough to string-match?
scenarios.question: How do you attach evidence?

options.name: Add `quote` and `source_id` fields to the JSON schema and verify quotes by string match
options.why: It works with structured output and lets code verify evidence for every field.
options.tradeoff: Quotes lengthen output and you maintain the verifier.

options.name: API-native citations in one call, then a second call to format as JSON
options.why: Keeps native span locations and valid JSON.
options.tradeoff: Two calls and extra latency and cost.

options.name: API-native citations together with structured outputs in one request
options.tradeoff: Right when the output is plain text, not structured.

flips.then: Use an entailment check instead of string match.

scenarios.takeaway: Pick the citation mechanism that your output format allows.

quiz.q: After enabling Anthropic citations on a request that also uses structured outputs, what happens?
quiz.explain: The documentation states the two features are incompatible and enabling both returns HTTP 400. Silent dropping and token doubling are not documented.

quiz.q: Which statement about citations is correct?
options: A citation proves the claim is true
A citation removes the need for abstention
A citation proves provenance, not that the passage entails the claim
A citation guarantees the retrieved set was complete
quiz.explain: A citation shows where text came from. Whether the span supports the claim needs a separate check, and completeness and abstention are unrelated to citing.

quiz.q: Order the steps of an evidence-enforced answer.
items: Check that cited spans support the claims
Answer or abstain with a next step
quiz.explain: Answerability comes before generation, and support checks come after, so unsupported text never reaches the user.

flashcards.back: A citation shows where text came from (provenance). Entailment asks whether the cited span supports the claim and needs its own check.

flashcards.front: Which Azure reranker facts matter for abstention thresholds?
flashcards.back: Scores run 0 to 4, only the top 50 candidates are reranked and distributions shift with model updates. Use coarse cut-offs and re-test.

flashcards.front: What do Anthropic citations not combine with?
flashcards.back: Structured outputs. Enabling both returns HTTP 400. They do work with prompt caching, token counting and batch.
